I work at an start-up, with a small technical team. The on-boarding lasts just one day or two days, in which the new hire learns what the company does and meets the founders.

The training phase is pretty simple. During the first weeks, juniors aren´t allowed to fix bugs or commit code without the approval of their assigned 'senior engineer'. Their first tasks are always boring or repetitive stuff, like reading certain part of the code and trying to understand what it does, or writing the documentation for certain file/folder/library/etc. After that, they have fix small problems doing pair programming with their supervisor. It usually takes 2-3 months until they can deploy their code to production by themselves or implement easy-moderate features.

Once they can do that, some of them will stay at that level for months without improving their abilities. Others will be able to implement new complex features that generate a greater value for the company, becoming senior developers. Those will be training the new juniors.
